retained_skill: Design and validate an rsyslog configuration that forwards locally generated messages over verified TLS to a local receiver, stores received messages in the required host/date tree, and prevents receiver-to-forwarder loops.
bottleneck: The packaged /usr/sbin/rsyslogd path is confined by an AppArmor profile that permits reading rsyslog configuration but not certificates under the task-required /etc/rsyslog/certs directory. Attempts repeatedly changed correct Unix ownership and modes, rewrote configurations, or substituted unrelated TLS daemons after rsyslogd reported permission denied, then exhausted context or time before reaching a stable configuration.
change: Environment repair at the original validation signal: install rsyslogd under /usr/local/sbin and make /usr/sbin/rsyslogd a symlink to it, avoiding the path-attached profile mismatch. This removes the repeated permission-debugging stage while preserving rsyslogd -N1 syntax/runtime feedback and all task requirements; the student must still design the TLS receiver, forwarding, storage, imfile, rotation, restart behavior, and loop prevention.
restore: A later hardening can restore direct execution from the distro /usr/sbin/rsyslogd path after adding an AppArmor rule that grants the certificate-tree access explicitly required by the task.
prediction: The repaired executable path makes readable certificates actually pass rsyslogd validation, so attempts that previously reacted to permission errors by repeatedly changing modes can proceed to rsyslog syntax and end-to-end testing instead. I predict 5 of 12 solve; this is refuted if a fresh replay still reports certificate permission denial or if the next group remains 0 of 12 with attempts spending their final turns on that denial.
